blurb: Arithmetic from the Peano axioms to ℤ, ℚ, ℝ, ℤ/nℤ, IEEE 754 floating point and O(n log n) multiplication.

pics.alt: Black-and-white photographic portrait of Giuseppe Peano, a bearded man in a dark jacket
pics.caption: Giuseppe Peano (1858–1932), whose Arithmetices principia (1889) set out the axioms for the natural numbers that bear his name. Together with Dedekind's work of 1888, it made arithmetic a deductive theory.
pics.title: Giuseppe Peano.jpg

pics.alt: Diagram of the 64 bits of an IEEE 754 double: 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits and 52 fraction bits, numbered 63 down to 0
pics.caption: The IEEE 754 binary64 (double-precision) format: bit 63 is the sign, bits 62–52 the biased exponent and bits 51–0 the fraction. With the hidden leading bit, the significand has 53 bits of precision.
pics.title: IEEE 754 Double Floating Point Format.svg
